title: Operator deletes a generated audio job
description:
An operator must be able to remove a generated clip and its audio artifact.
Today nothing in the system can delete a job: `grep` for delete across the
repo returns only `_delete_site`. Audio accumulates in S3 forever.

Deleting a job also deletes its S3 object. A subsequent `POST /jobs` for the
same content hash is then a clean create, which makes delete the crude form
of regeneration (the deliberate form is auritus-<regenerate>).

## Feature

```gherkin
Feature: Deleting a generated audio job

  Scenario: Operator deletes a completed job and its audio
    Given a job exists with status "done" and a stored audio object
    When the operator deletes the job by content hash
    Then the job record is removed
    And the audio object is removed from the audio bucket
    And requesting that job returns not found

  Scenario: Deleting a job frees the content hash for regeneration
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When the operator deletes the job by content hash
    And the embed requests audio for the same content
    Then a new job is created with status "pending"

  Scenario: Deleting a job that does not exist
    When the operator deletes a content hash with no job record
    Then the response is not found
    And no audio object is removed

  Scenario: Deleting a job requires operator authentication
    Given a job exists with status "done"
    When a caller presents only a site key and deletes the job
    Then the response is forbidden
    And the job record still exists
```

## Implementation brief

**`cdk/lambdas/router/handler.py`**

- Add route dispatch: `if method == "DELETE" and path.startswith("/admin/jobs/")`
  -> `_delete_admin_job(content_hash, headers)`. Place it before the existing
  `GET /admin/jobs/` prefix check is irrelevant (different method), but keep
  it grouped with the other admin routes.
- `def _delete_admin_job(content_hash: str, headers: dict[str, str]) -> dict[str, Any]:`
  - `_require_operator(headers)`
  - `item = _jobs.get_item(Key={"content_hash": content_hash}).get("Item")`;
    raise `LookupError("job_not_found")` when absent.
  - When `item.get("audio_key")`, call
    `_s3.delete_object(Bucket=AUDIO_BUCKET, Key=item["audio_key"])`. Tolerate
    a missing object (S3 delete is idempotent); do not swallow other errors.
  - `_jobs.delete_item(Key={"content_hash": content_hash})`
  - Return `_response(200, {"content_hash": content_hash, "deleted": True})`

**`cdk/stacks/backend.py`** — the router Lambda's role currently has read/write
on the audio bucket via the existing grant; confirm `s3:DeleteObject` is
included and add `audio_bucket.grant_delete(router_lambda)` if not.

**`cli/src/auritus/api.py`** — add
`def delete_job(self, content_hash: str) -> dict[str, Any]` calling
`self._request("DELETE", f"/admin/jobs/{content_hash}")`.

**`features/`** — new `job_management.feature` carrying the scenarios above,
with steps in `features/steps/`.

## Acceptance

`make check` green, and the Gherkin scenarios above pass against the router
handler.
